turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to come see me?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Doctor. Thank you. 

Well, I'm here because... I'm having a really hard time at work. I'm a building cleaner, and lately, just the thought of seeing a rat has gotten so bad that I can't even do parts of my job anymore. I mean, I know it's probably just an old building or a trash room I need to empty, and it's not really dangerous, but... I just can't make myself go in there. It's getting to be a real problem.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient reports a marked fear of seeing rats that they acknowledge is out of proportion to the actual danger.
symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient actively avoids entering trash rooms or areas where they fear encountering rats, impairing their ability to do their job.

turns.doctor_question: When you're not at work or not thinking about going into those areas, do you find yourself having unwanted thoughts or images about rats that just pop into your head and bother you?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. Um, if I'm at home or just doing my own thing, I don't really think about them. It's not like images of them just pop into my head out of nowhere. 

It's really only when I'm at work, or... well, when I know I have to go into those specific areas. As long as I'm away from all that and not thinking about my shift, I'm pretty much fine.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly denies having unwanted thoughts or images popping into their head when away from work or the specific phobic situation.

turns.doctor_question: When you're in those areas at work where you might encounter a rat, or even just thinking about going there, what happens in your body? Do you notice things like your heart racing, sweating, trembling, or feeling like you can't breathe?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it does. If I hear even just a little scratching sound near a wall, or see something move by a pipe, my whole body reacts right away. My heart starts pounding, my hands shake... and I just feel like I have to get out of there before I can even think straight. It just happens instantly.

symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient describes an immediate physiological fear response occurring instantly upon cues of a rat, including a pounding heart, trembling hands, and an urgent urge to flee.

turns.doctor_question: When you know you're going to work, do you deliberately plan your day or make changes to avoid going into those areas where rats might be, or does the avoidance just happen naturally when you get there?
turns.patient_response:
I definitely plan ahead. Whenever I can, I turn down any cleaning routes that include basements, storage rooms, laundry areas, or having to go out to the alley dumpsters. I just try to get out of doing them completely. 

But if I'm forced to clean one of those spots and I can't avoid it, I always make sure to prop the door wide open. I just rush through the work as fast as I possibly can, and honestly, I'm pretty much scared the entire time I'm in there.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient actively plans ahead to avoid areas associated with rats and, when unavoidable, endures cleaning them with safety behaviors and persistent fear.
